passage: I'm Jasleen. At recess I saw three boys empty a smaller boy's pencil box into the dustbin, and I could not stop thinking about it all through Hindi class. I was scared people would call me a snitch. After the bell I waited until the room was empty and went to Rajni Ma'am's desk. "Ma'am, can I tell you something? Please don't say it was me." She listened and nodded. She said she would deal with it in a way that did not point to me. I walked home relieved but a little shaky. Later I decided that speaking up to keep someone safe is a different thing from tattling.

qa.q: What did the three boys do to the smaller boy's pencil box?
qa.a: They emptied it into the dustbin at recess.

qa.q: What was Jasleen worried about before she went to the teacher?
qa.a: Jasleen was afraid other students would find out and call Jasleen a snitch.

qa.q: How can a teacher make it safer for a child like Jasleen to speak up?
qa.a: The teacher can listen, keep the child's name private and deal with it without pointing at the child, as Rajni Ma'am promised.

qa.q: How might the smaller boy be affected by Jasleen speaking up?
qa.a: He may be protected without having to report it himself, since the teacher can step in to stop the three boys.

grounding: A bystander quietly tells the teacher what was seen, worrying about being called a snitch.

passage:
I'm Vidya, and in Class 5 I saw something I couldn't forget. Behind the library, two boys took Vaibhav's lunch box and ate his food while he watched, silent.
I thought about it all afternoon. If I told, would everyone call me a snitch?
At home I kept thinking: telling to protect someone isn't the same as getting someone in trouble for fun.
Next morning, before class, I went to Mrs Lobo. "Ma'am, can I tell you something privately?" I told her.
She thanked me and promised she wouldn't use my name. That afternoon, the boys were called to the office. No one ever found out it was me.

qa.q: Where did the boys take Vaibhav's lunch box?

qa.a: Vidya was worried about being called a snitch for telling.

qa.q: Why was telling Mrs Lobo the right choice?
qa.a: Vidya was protecting Vaibhav from harm, not trying to get anyone in trouble, and Mrs Lobo acted while keeping the name private.

qa.q: How might Mrs Lobo see Vidya's choice to tell?
qa.a: Mrs Lobo sees it as brave and responsible, which is why she thanks Vidya and protects the name.

grounding: A child quietly tells a teacher about bullying they witnessed, worried about being a snitch, and the teacher keeps their name private.

passage:
Note from the class teacher, Friday.
Deepika stayed back after the last bell today, twisting her dupatta. She told me, in a whisper, that she had seen three girls from the back bench tear up Vidya's homework and throw it in the dustbin. "Please don't tell them it was me. They'll call me a snitch," she said.
I told her that speaking up to keep someone safe is not tattling, and that her name would stay with me.
I spoke to the three girls on Monday morning without saying how I knew. I also checked on Vidya. Deepika looked relieved in class.

qa.q: What did Deepika see the three girls do with Vidya's homework?
qa.a: She saw them tear up Vidya's homework and throw it in the dustbin.

qa.q: What was Deepika feeling when she spoke in a whisper?
qa.a: She was nervous and scared of being called a snitch, twisting her dupatta.

qa.q: What did the teacher do that made telling safe?
qa.a: The teacher reassured Deepika that protecting someone isn't tattling, kept her name private, and acted without saying how they knew.

qa.q: How might Vidya feel when the teacher checks on her?
qa.a: Vidya may feel noticed and supported, knowing an adult is watching out for her.

grounding: A girl quietly tells her teacher about bullying she saw, fearing she will be called a snitch; the teacher keeps her name private and acts.
